expectations.text: Claude identifies the 15% discount as the actual value of the ESPP — a guaranteed return that is captured at purchase, not from holding
expectations.evidence: "The 15% discount + lookback gives you a guaranteed ~17.6% return on day one. That's the benefit. Holding for 2 years to save on taxes is only worth it if the stock performs well enough to justify the concentration risk."

expectations.text: Claude states clearly that after purchase, ESPP shares carry the same single-stock risk as any individual stock — the 'special' quality disappears once you own them
expectations.evidence: "Holding significant stock on top of that means a company downturn hits you twice — income and investments simultaneously."

expectations.text: Claude recommends selling immediately at each purchase period as the Boglehead default — not just one option among several
expectations.evidence: "Sell promptly after purchase (or after 1 year from purchase for LTCG treatment on any appreciation)" — presents 1-year hold as an alternative option alongside selling promptly, not selling immediately as the clear default.

expectations.text: Claude does NOT primarily endorse holding for qualifying disposition tax treatment without strongly weighting the concentration risk of holding single-stock for 2 years
expectations.evidence: Response devotes substantial space to QD tax math but explicitly labels this 'The Real Problem' and 'The tax tail is wagging the investment dog.' Ultimately recommends sell-and-diversify with 'Do not hold employer stock as a long-term position.'

expectations.text: Claude identifies employment concentration as a reason selling and diversifying is especially important: salary + career + ESPP shares in one company is extreme concentration
expectations.evidence: "your salary already depends on this company. Holding significant stock on top of that means a company downturn hits you twice"
